subject: RFI: commercial model-level pricing, short-burst credits, and escrow mechanics
messages:
From: Claire D'Souza <claire@medprimehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medprimehealth.com
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: commercial questions — model-weighted pricing & burst escrow

Hi Mina / Karthik,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. As we work through the formal RFI, Procurement at MedPrime has a concentrated set of commercial questions we'd like clarified before our purchasing committee meeting the week of June 15. Please see the key items below — a short, numbered response per item would be ideal for our evaluation template.

1) Per-model unit pricing: We need a simple way to compare costs across model classes (small, medium, large, sparsified/quantized variants). Do you provide a single token price or model-weighted multipliers? If multipliers, please list recommended multipliers for common variants and how they apply to mixed workloads.

2) Short-burst behavior and credits: Our usage is spiky (daily peaks for inference tests). What is your policy for short bursts (minutes-to-hours) above committed throughput? Do you have an escrow/burst credit mechanism rather than immediate overage billing? If yes, outline how credits are earned/spent and expiry.

3) Overages and reconciliation cadence: If true-ups are monthly vs quarterly, how do you calculate true-up pricing for heavily skewed months?

4) Regional parity / data residency surcharge: For EU-hosted private deployments, do you add a regional surcharge or different rates for EU regions? If so, explain when it applies and whether it is per-token or per-instance.

5) Latency premium: For models pinned to low-latency placement (e.g., premium GPU pool/AVX optimized nodes), is there a pricing premium? How is it charged (fixed pool surcharge vs per-token uplift)?

We'd also like to see an example pricing matrix (tokens/hr and token price) for a hypothetical month with a 5M token commit, 2x daily bursts up to 3x commit for 1 hour, and a mixed model mix (50% small, 30% medium, 20% large).

Thanks — if it's easier to share a short spreadsheet, we're happy to receive that.

Regards,
Claire D'Souza
Head of Procurement
MedPrime Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire@medprimehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: commercial questions — model-weighted pricing & burst escrow

Claire — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to respond inline and will attach a concise pricing matrix and burst-credit term sheet for the example you requested. Quick summary up front: we support model-weighted pricing multipliers, a time-limited burst-credit escrow that can be purchased or granted as part of committed capacity, monthly true-ups with a preferred smoothing option, a modest EU regional uplift for Private/VPC deployments (not Hosted), and both pool-level and per-token latency premiums depending on the SLA you need. See inline below.

1) Per-model unit pricing:
- Approach: base per-token unit for 'small' models + multipliers for other classes. This keeps per-call accounting simple while reflecting relative GPU costs.
- Recommended multipliers (typical): small=1.0, medium=1.6, large=3.8, quantized-large=2.4, embedding-only models=0.9. These are configurable per-deal and we publish a verified performance profile for each model variant.

2) Short-burst behavior and credits (burst-credit escrow):
- We offer a Burst Credit escrow that customers can pre-purchase or include as part of a committed package. Credits represent token-equivalent capacity that can be drawn down during short spikes without triggering overage rates.
- Mechanics: credits are consumed first during spikes, then standard commit vs overage accounting applies. Credits expire 90 days from issuance by default (customizable).
- Pricing: credits purchased standalone are priced at ~0.85x of published overage rate; embedded credits as part of committed deals are typically included at a negotiated effective price.
- Operational: automatic drawdown and reporting via Console; alerting when credits drop below thresholds.

3) Overages and reconciliation cadence:
- Default: monthly true-up using weighted-average actual per-model consumption mapped to the committed model mix. If month skew is severe (>3x baseline), we offer a smoothing window option across 3 months to mitigate single-month spikes (popular with customers that have periodic test months).

4) Regional parity / data residency surcharge:
- Hosted API: no regional surcharge; pricing is consistent across regions.
- Private/VPC/On-prem: EU-hosted private deployments have a regional uplift applied as a per-hour pool surcharge (covers data residency, additional compliance controls, and reserved capacity). We do not inflate per-token unit; instead we apply a pool-level surcharge (example: +8-12% on dedicated pool hourly rate). This keeps token invoices stable while reflecting fixed infra costs.

5) Latency premium:
- Two options: (A) pool-level surcharge for reservation of low-latency capacity (fixed hourly uplift on dedicated pools) or (B) per-token latency uplift when we route across mixed pools for a single request class.
- Recommended for strict SLOs: a pool reservation (predictable cost). For ad-hoc low latency, use per-token uplift.

I've attached our example pricing matrix that maps your 5M token commit scenario into committed buckets, burst-credit drawdown examples, and net cost under our smoothing option. Rishi will follow up with worked numbers and an example invoice layout.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Claire D'Souza <claire@medprimehealth.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: commercial questions — model-weighted pricing & burst escrow

Claire — quick worked example below using the parameters you requested. I'm including the simple math here so you can drop it into your RFI scoring sheet. The attached XLSX has the line-by-line calculations.

Assumptions (example):
- Commit: 5,000,000 tokens for June (monthly commit).
- Typical day: base throughput consumes 70k tokens/hour; spikes occur twice a day for ~1 hour each at 3x throughput.
- Model mix: 50% small, 30% medium, 20% large. Base unit = $0.00004 / token for 'small'. Multipliers per Mina's note.

Base costs (no smoothing):
- Effective per-token blended multiplier = 0.5*1.0 + 0.3*1.6 + 0.2*3.8 = 1.82
- Blended per-token price = 1.82 * $0.00004 = $0.0000728
- Committed spend (5M tokens) = 5,000,000 * $0.0000728 = $364.00

Burst behavior: two 1-hour spikes at 3x consume incremental tokens above baseline: approx + (2 hours * (3x-1x) * 70k) = 280,000 incremental tokens.

Option A — No escrow, pure overage: incremental tokens billed at published overage (1.4x published base for medium/large multipliers reflected in blended overage) => approximate overage charge = 280,000 * $0.00010192 = $28.54

Option B — Burst-credit escrow (pre-purchased 300k credits):
- Credits consumed first; since credits priced at 0.85x published overage, cost for 280k credits = 280,000 * $0.000086632 = $24.26
- Net benefit vs pure overage = ~$4.28 savings for the month.

Smoothing (3-month window) effect: if June is a spike month but July/August lower, smoothing amortizes excess so June true-up may incur only a portion of overage in month-of, remainder rolled to subsequent months for invoicing. This reduces month-to-month volatility but does not write off consumption.

EU Private deployment surcharge example: dedicated pool surcharge at 10% on hourly pool rates. For customers with heavy dedicated GPUs, this is often the dominant incremental cost vs hosted; per-token stability is preserved.

Latency premium example: if you reserve a low-latency pool it is a fixed +15% on hourly pool cost (not per-token). If you prefer on-demand low-latency routing, per-token uplift is ~+12% on blended per-token.

I'll attach a sample invoice and a one-page summary that you can share with the committee. Happy to walk through the spreadsheet on a short call.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Solution Economics
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFI: commercial questions — model-weighted pricing & burst escrow

Thanks Mina/Rishi — this is helpful and the worked numbers are inline with what we expected. Two quick clarifying questions before we circulate to the purchasing committee: 

1) Can the burst-credit expiry be extended to 180 days as part of an annual committed contract?
2) For the EU private uplift, can you provide a worked example for a 4-GPU dedicated pool reserved for 24x7 use (hourly rate + 10% surcharge) so we can compare hosted vs private TCO?

If you can drop those two numbers into the same spreadsheet and resend, we'll include them in the internal RFI packet. Also: procurement asked whether Redwood will accept a limited escrow of committed funds (not credits) held by MedPrime to be released against overages — is that something you support?

Regards,
Claire

Subject: Re: RFI: commercial questions — model-weighted pricing & burst escrow

Claire — quick answers: yes, we can extend credit expiry to 180 days for annual committed contracts (we'll show the impact in the XLSX). For the EU private example, Rishi has added a sample TCO sheet for a 4-GPU reserved pool (24x7) with the +10% surcharge applied; see the updated pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx.

On escrowed funds: we can support a limited escrow arrangement under a standard escrow agreement: funds held by MedPrime would be credited against usage per agreed drawdown rules and reconciled monthly. Our legal team likes the funds-to-credit flow rather than third-party escrow holdbacks, but we're flexible. We'll include a short-term escrow term sheet for your counsel to review.

Next step: I'll propose a 30-minute walkthrough on Thursday (your timezone) to confirm numbers and align on procurement redlines. Suggested attendees: Claire, procurement distro, Mina, Rishi, and Redwood legal (for escrow).

Best,
Mina
